thread:
maria_support: FYI Brightleaf just opened a ticket — their API calls to our private endpoint are getting 403s from their firewall after a NAT change on their side. They say it started ~ 2024-11-01 02:10 UTC. Pasting their curl output below.

eli_brightleaf (copied in their ticket): `curl -v https://api.private.redwood.company/health -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\"` -> response 403. Customer logs show requests arriving from 18.195.72.120 and 3.229.14.9 intermittently.

maria_support: Can someone confirm if we rotated any outbound IPs on our Private control plane or if there's any NAT change on our side? Customer is blocked by a static allowlist.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance: NAT gateway replacement in us-east-1 completed 2024-10-31T22:43:00Z. New public addresses allocated. (ticket #INF-2024-582) :gear:

jon_network: Looking. The Private control plane did rotate a managed NAT gateway in that region during the maintenance window — that affected control plane egress IPs for some VPC connectors. That would change source SNAT for our side (not customer VPC).

sam_sre: Clarifying question — is the customer behind our Private connector (we proxy) or are they calling our public hosted API from their VPC? Maria, which is it?

maria_support: They are on Private (VPC peering + our connector). They expected a fixed egress address we supplied previously. They said the allowlist was last updated 2024-09-12.

jon_network: Ok that explains it. When we replaced the NAT gateway we reallocated a new Elastic IP pool for that connector. I can pull the old vs new mapping. Stand by.

jon_network: Old SNATs for connector-ble-01: [34.82.11.5, 34.82.11.6] -> New SNATs: [18.195.72.120, 3.229.14.9]. Customer's firewall still allows only the old 34.82.11.5/6.

maria_support: Ugh — they blocked us. Customer says they didn't get a heads up. How did that happen?

jon_network: This was a planned behind-the-scenes migration (IP deprecations) but we failed to notify Private customers that had static allowlists tied to those specific EIPs. Action: we need to provide immediate mitigation steps.

sam_sre: Short-term mitigation: ask Brightleaf to add the new SNAT addresses to their allowlist. Long-term: we should offer a static EIP mapping addon or document TTL and rotation policy.

maria_support: I messaged Brightleaf with the new IPs and asked them to whitelist. They're requesting a repro path to confirm once done.

jon_network: For repro they can curl our endpoint from their app and echo the source IP we see in request headers. We add this header for Private connector traffic: `X-Redwood-Source-IP: <observed-snat>` — sample:
```
> curl -s -D - https://api.private.redwood.company/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
HTTP/2 200
X-Redwood-Source-IP: 18.195.72.120
...body...
```

maria_support: Brightleaf ran the test and pasted results — still 403 after adding the two IPs, they see X-Redwood-Source-IP: 18.195.72.120 in the response header.

jon_network: If they already whitelisted the new IPs and still see 403, possibilities: 1) They whitelisted only one IP but our outgoing is round-robin across both; 2) Their firewall caches allowlist changes (check TTL), 3) They have Geo/IP block lists blocking AWS ranges. Ask them to temporarily allow the whole /32 entries we provided.

sam_sre: Also confirm there's no TLS SNI mismatch or host header rewrite. 403 in their logs indicates firewall dropped the connection before it reached our infra. Their firewall should log the observed source IP and SNI — ask them for firewall logs for the hit timestamps.

maria_support: Transcribed reply from Brightleaf: "We added both IPs, waits 5m, still 403. Firewall logs show connection attempt from 18.195.72.120 to our public IP and rule 'deny' matched — reason: source IP not in allowlist (we only added 18.195.72.120, not 3.229.14.9)."

jon_network: So they only added one. Confirmed multi-IP egress. Ask them to add both and validate.

maria_support: Done. Also requesting a post-mortem and a permanent option so this doesn't happen again with other Private customers.

jon_network: Agreed. Post-mortem notes: 1) Lack of outbound IP rotation notif to Private customers. 2) Missing documented SLA for static EIP mapping for connectors. 3) Need an automated webhook/email to affected customers when NAT changes for their connector.

sam_sre: As an immediate follow-up I'll open ENG-OPS ticket to add a 'static-egress' flag for connectors and add a migration checklist to notify customers when maintenance will change SNATs.

infra-bot: New ticket created ENG-OPS-2024-993: add static egress option + notify flow.

maria_support: Brightleaf confirmed whitelist update for both IPs and says 200s now — they validated the curl returns 200 and X-Redwood-Source-IP alternates between the two. Closing the immediate support ticket. :white_check_mark:

jon_network: For the post-mortem I'll include a suggested customer communication template and rollout plan.

sam_sre: Also let's add a short KB article under Private -> Networking describing: how to verify observed egress (X-Redwood-Source-IP), expected rotation policy (EIP rotations happen for maintenance, typical window), and recommended allowlist guidance (allow both current SNATs or request static-egress).

maria_support: Thanks team. I'll update the ticket with the mitigation steps and link to ENG-OPS-2024-993.

jon_network: +1. Leaving notes for oncall if this reoccurs.

maria_support: Closing thread here.
